newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK's Hang Seng Index set for shuffle - analysts.
newsitem.headline: HK's Hang Seng Index set for shuffle - analysts.

text.p: The growing weight of China-related stocks in the Hong Kong market is likely to lead to a shuffle in the blue-chip Hang Seng Index soon to include the territory's biggest red chips, analysts said on Monday.
"I expect that there will definitely be some reshuffling in the Hang Seng Index after the handover," said Kelvin Tang, an analyst at ImPac Asset Management (HK) Ltd.
"After 1997, the market structure in Hong Kong might change a bit so the index should reflect the economic structure and the whole stock market structure," he said.

China plays have been a strong investment theme in the run-up to Hong Kong's return to Chinese rule on July 1, driving the market capitalisations of some of these companies to higher levels than some of the current blue chips.
Daily market turnover in red chips -- Hong Kong incorporated companies with mainland financial backing -- has sometimes outweighed turnover in the main blue chips over recent weeks.
"The Hang Seng Index right now no longer represents the Hong Kong market as closely as in the past," said Frederick Tsang, head of research at BNP PrimeEast Securities.
HSI Services Ltd, the keeper of the Hang Seng Index, says the 33-company blue chip index represents more than 70 percent of Hong Kong's market capitalisation.

"Our study last month indicated that the HSI representation had dropped quite severely," said Tsang. "We found out that as of the end of April, the HSI now only accounts for 62 percent of the market cap size and 40 percent of trading volume."
He said red chips collectively represented about six percent of Hong Kong's market capitalisation at the end of April.
The Hang Seng Index already includes two red chips, CITIC Pacific Ltd and Guangdong Investment Ltd.
The most likely candidate to join next is China Resources Enterprise Ltd, with a market capitalisation of HK$30-35 billion (US$3.9-4.5 billion), analysts said.

Another red chip favourite, Shanghai Industrial Holdings Ltd, also has a market capitalisation of HK$30-35 billion, but since it has only been listed in Hong Kong for less than one year, it may not be chosen immediately, analysts said.

An Lu, vice president at Salomon Brothers, said he expected a shuffle in the index around the handover period. "The more actively traded like China Resources and Shanghai Industrial need to find a place there to make it more representative."
HSI Services considers index shuffling a sensitive topic and declined to comment on the issue. "HSI reviews the Hang Seng Index on a quarterly basis," spokesman Tony Chiu said.
The last time the components of the Hang Seng Index were shuffled was in August 1996.
But HSI Services has responded to the increasing interest in China-related stocks with a plan to launch a red chip index.

Chiu said HSI would choose the stocks for the new index based on their level of Chinese ownership. He said it may be possible to have stocks included in both the Hang Seng Index and the new China-play index. "We do not exclude the possibility that there can be overlapping stocks," he said.
HSI Services has yet to fix a percentage for the level of ownership and a name for the indexh, but the barometer would be launched as soon as possible, Chiu said.
"It will be a very important benchmark for a lot of people to value red chips in the future. You cannot afford to ignore a sector which accounts for so much of turnover," said Lu of Salomon Brothers.
